## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the competitive game to offer an endless continuation option beyond the win threshold (producer Q4: “option to carry on in endless mode”), so we can keep building after someone wins.

## Context

Competitive mode's win condition is first-to-threshold (parent CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30, phase-machine sibling). The producer explicitly asked for an endless continuation beyond threshold. Planning deferred this to a separate top-level issue (not a child of the competitive epic) so the competitive epic stays engine-focused and endless mode can land independently. N-player-ready design (PlayerRecord[]) is already in scope for the competitive architecture.

## Scope

- Endless-mode trigger and state handling after the win threshold is first reached (continue playing beyond threshold; scoring/phase semantics while beyond threshold).
- How the UI/scene signals “winner declared but still playing” (if any UI is needed here; full competitive rendering is the separate CG-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K child).
- Whether endless mode needs its own Monte Carlo treatment or is validated by manual play.

## Out of scope

- Competitive state model / phase machine / income routing / AI / harness / rendering — those are CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 and its children.
- Denial reasoning (separate follow-up).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Endless mode wiring is defined via an explicit opt-in flag/config: what triggers continuation, what happens to win detection/score/endReason/gameResult when play continues beyond threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Deterministic behaviour — same seed + same actions produce the same endless-mode outcome.
- [ ] **AC3:** Competitive mode remains playable without engaging endless mode (players can stop at the threshold win; default behaviour unchanged).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Endless-mode flag/state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Win detection vs. continue-beyond-threshold semantics.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-endless.test.ts` — Dedicated endless-mode tests (threshold win vs. continuation).

## Related Work

- Producer Q4 (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30): “when one player reaches a win condition with option to carry on in endless mode” — now tracked here.
- Parent competitive epic: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 (first-to-threshold is the win condition; this issue layers continuation beyond it).
- Competitive rendering child: CG-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K — visual winner/continuation affordance.
- Competitive state/phase siblings on CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30.

# Intake Brief — Move level label to left (MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327)

## Problem Statement
When a business or community-space card is upgraded it shows a gold level badge
("Lvl 1", "Lvl 2", …) in the **top-right** corner of the card face. This
position competes with the cost circle / right-hand text column and reads as a
secondary stat rather than the card's primary upgrade indicator. The badge
should move to the **top-left** of the card so the upgrade level is immediately
visible in a consistent, expected position.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants to identify an upgraded card's level at a
  glance when scanning the street grid and their hand.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse the shared
  `UpgradeOverlaySpec` contract and expect a single, predictable corner
  convention for the level badge.

### User Stories
- As a player, when I look at an upgraded card on the street or in my hand, I
  see the "Lvl N" badge at the top-left of the card, so the level is obvious at
  a glance.
- As a player, the badge position is identical whether the card is shown on the
  street grid or in the hand, so I never have to re-learn where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For every upgraded card (`level > 0`), the level badge is positioned at
      the card's **top-left**: in container-local coordinates (origin at the
      card centre) `levelBadge.x` is negative (left of centre) and the badge is
      **left-anchored** (`originX === 0`); the badge is no longer placed in the
      top-right (`x` must not be positive in the mirrored position). Verified by
      unit test on `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` for level 1 and level 2 cards.
- [ ] The Phaser renderer (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) renders the badge with a
      left/top origin so the text starts at the top-left inset and remains fully
      inside the card bounds (no clipping past the left or top edge); the same
      overlay path is used by street and hand cards, so both move together.
      Verified by renderer/overlay tests.
- [ ] Badge content and styling are unchanged (`Lvl N`, gold `#ffdd44`, bold,
      10px) and no badge is produced for level 0 (base) cards.
- [ ] The dynamic SVG card-face generator (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits the
      level badge at the top-left (`x` at the card's left inset,
      `text-anchor="start"`) for consistency with the overlay, with its unit
      tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the module docs in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` /
      `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and the level-badge references in
      `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with all existing
      top-right level-badge expectations updated to the top-left contract.

## Constraints
- Card geometry is fixed: canonical **140 × 80** card with a **64 × 64 art zone
  at (8, 8)** (top-left) — see `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`. The
  top-left corner is therefore occupied by the card art; the badge will render
  over the top-left of the art zone (mirroring the current badge overlaying the
  top-right). This is an accepted input to the brief (see Risks & Assumptions).
- Presentation-only change — no change to upgrade rules, card state, or level
  numbers.
- Reuse the existing overlay/badge primitives and gold styling; do not introduce
  new assets or a second badge component.
- Keep the overlay spec a pure data module (no Phaser imports) so it stays
  unit-testable in Node.

## Existing State
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` builds the badge at
  `x = Math.round(width / 2 - 4)`, `y = Math.round(4 - height / 2)` (top-right,
  4 px inset) with `color: '#ffdd44'`, `fontSize: '10px'`, `fontStyle: 'bold'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) creates the
  Phaser Text and calls `lvlText.setOrigin(1, 0)` — right/top anchored — so the
  badge sits in the top-right.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits
  `<text x="${width - 8}" y="13" … text-anchor="end">Lvl N</text>` (top-right)
  for upgraded cards. (This dynamic SVG path is exercised by unit tests; the
  runtime card face texture comes from the CSV-based template SVGs.)
- Tests asserting/pinning the badge: `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts`
  (positions the badge in the top-right), `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts`
  and `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (badge presence/text),
  `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` (badge text).

## Desired Change
- Mirror the badge to the top-left: overlay `x = Math.round(-width / 2 + 4)`
  with `originX: 0` (and `setOrigin(0, 0)` in the renderer); `y` stays at the
  existing top inset so the badge remains on the top edge.
- Update the SVG generator badge to `x = 8` (or the chosen left inset) with
  `text-anchor="start"`.
- Update the module/JSDoc comments and the affected tests from "top-right" to
  "top-left". Exact inset values may be tuned during implementation as long as
  the badge is left-anchored in the top-left and stays inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — level-badge spec `x` / `originX` and the
  "top-right corner" comment; primary change.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays` badge
  `setOrigin(1, 0)` → `(0, 0)`; comment.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — dynamic SVG badge position /
  `text-anchor`; module doc mentions "level badge top-right".
- `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` — update the top-right
  position assertion to top-left and assert left-anchoring.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — badge position/style
  expectations.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — badge presence/absence
  alongside the cash line (position regression surface).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — SVG badge text/position.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — level-badge placement references.

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — canonical 140×80 card and the
    `(8, 8)` 64×64 art zone that occupies the top-left.
  - `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — upgrade level-up burst notes that
    reference the newly-rendered level badge.
  - `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` header — documents the overlay contract
    and the card-local coordinate system.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — *Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card,
    growing right* (bug, medium) — closest precedent: a card-face overlay
    repositioned from centre/right to left, landed with documented placement
    assumptions.
  - `MS-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J` — *Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored
    position* (task) — companion implementation task for the sister reposition.
  - `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — *Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main
    Street card* (medium) — touches the top-left art zone that the badge will
    now overlay.
  - `MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R` — *Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to
    Physiotherapist* (task, low) — another card-face presentation tweak with
    test/doc churn.
  - Historical (core-repo) references cited in code: `CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`
    (64×64 left-art layout) and `CG-0MP1VJVEK003I7VE` (display upgrade state on
    street-grid cards) — the layout and overlay these tests assert were
    introduced/refined there.
- **Automated report** (generated by `find-related`) — see the
  "Related work (automated report)" section retained below.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Assumption:** "top left" means the card's top-left corner, mirroring the
  current right-side inset, with the badge left-aligned. Because the 64×64 art
  zone occupies `(8, 8)`–`(72, 72)`, the badge will overlay the top-left of the
  card art. That is accepted; if the producer finds it illegible over the art, a
  subtle backing chip or a slightly different inset is a small follow-up — it
  must be raised rather than assumed.
- **Visual-regression risk:** the badge colour (`#ffdd44` gold) may have low
  contrast against some card art; mitigate during implementation by checking the
  darkest/lightest card arts and, if needed, a 1 px dark outline (recorded as a
  follow-up if it expands scope).
- **Test churn:** `upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` explicitly asserts a
  top-right position; update the assertions to the top-left contract in the same
  change rather than deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the badge, redesign the 64×64 layout, or
  change the cost circle / title / cash line. Record any broader card-face polish
  as separate work items.

## Open Questions
- None — the seed context (position the upgrade level badge at the top-left
  instead of the top-right) plus repo inspection of the overlay/spec/renderer
  provided sufficient signal for a clear brief. The only judgement call (badge
  overlays the top-left art zone) is recorded above as an assumption to be
  confirmed during review; no clarifying interview was required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work-item description ("When a card is upgraded
  it gets a 'Lvl 1' label. Move this from the current location (top right) to
  the top left.") plus repo inspection of `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`,
  `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, and `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` provided
  sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left
  unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for the documented top-left-art-overlay
  assumption.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MUB0GFY00001ASV** – write storylines (open)
- **MS-0MTIILDBB001F01S** – Competitive Monte Carlo harness: head-to-head simulation (blocked)
- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** – Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, location, lvl, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `core/docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — matched: card, current, gets, left, level, location, move, right, top, upgraded, when
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: card, current, gets, label, left, level, move, right, top, upgraded, when

# Add test cases for AI and human win threshold in competitive mode

## Summary
Add test cases to `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-harness-smoke.test.ts` covering: (a) AI reaches threshold → human loss; (b) human reaches threshold → human win; (c) multi-AI scenario with human losing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — AI threshold win test:** A test using `buildHumanVsAis()` that sets an AI player's score ≥ `winThreshold` and asserts `gameResult === 'loss'` and `competitiveWinnerId === <ai_index>` when `checkCompetitiveEndConditions` is called.

2. **AC2 — Human threshold win test:** A test using `buildHumanVsAis()` that sets the human player's score ≥ `winThreshold` and asserts `gameResult === 'win'` and `competitiveWinnerId === <human_index>`.

3. **AC3 — Multi-AI threshold test:** A test with human + multiple AIs where the highest-scoring AI wins, asserting `gameResult === 'loss'` for the human and correct `competitiveWinnerId`.

4. **AC4 — All existing tests pass:** No regressions in the existing test suite.

## Implementation Notes

- Use existing test harness from `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts` (`buildHumanVsAis()`, `evaluateEndConditions()`).
- These tests must be added before the implementation fix so they initially fail, confirming the bug.
- The `findHumanSeatId()` helper exists and returns the human's index in `state.players` or -1.
- Key file: `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-harness-smoke.test.ts`

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/competitive-end-condition-harness-smoke.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` (reference for `checkCompetitiveEndConditions`)

# Intake Brief — Card-level unit and browser integration test framework with CSV result reporting

**Headline:** Build an automated per-card verification mechanism that exercises all 174 Main Street cards through real play states (unit integration) and the real Phaser scene (browser integration), asserting expected discounts/buffs/effects and recording pass/fail plus failure notes back into `src/card-data.csv`.

## Problem statement

Card behaviour — especially staff discounts (`purchaseCostDiscount`, `upgradeCostDiscount`, `refreshCostDiscount`), action/peek/hand-slot staff abilities, and event/business/upgrade effects — can silently diverge from what `card-data.csv` declares. There is no systematic proof that each card, when bought and/or played on a particular board, produces the expected change in game state. Manual spot-checks and balance tooling do not catch regressions in individual cards.

## Users

- **Game designer / producer** — needs confidence that a CSV edit reaches the engine and the UI correctly.
- **Developer** — needs a fast, deterministic regression guard that pinpoints the failing card and the reason.
- **QA** — needs a per-card pass/fail record for release sign-off.

Example user stories:
- As a designer, when I change a staff card's `purchaseCostDiscount`, I want a test that proves the discounted cost is charged end to end.
- As a developer, when I add a new card to `card-data.csv`, I want to add one test definition and have it discovered, executed, and reported automatically.
- As QA, when a card fails, I want a machine-readable note of the observed vs expected game state in the CSV.

## Acceptance criteria (epic)

1. A card test framework parses `src/card-data.csv` and discovers all 174 cards (31 business, 8 community-space, 39 upgrade, 25 staff, 71 event); a card with no registered definition is reported as a failure, never silently skipped.
2. A **unit integration** suite (Node/Vitest) tests every card against real play states and turn progressions: controlled state via `setupMainStreetGame`, card acquired/played through real engine APIs, turns advanced, resulting state asserted.
3. A **browser integration** suite (Vitest/Playwright, headless Chromium) tests every card through the real `MainStreetScene`, asserting player-facing UI/state (HUD, activity log, market/hand, applied discount values).
4. Staff cards (the discount/buff-bearing family) receive up to **3 combination tests** each, covering discount stacking, per-business vs street-wide scoping, and synergy/upgrade interaction.
5. Results are written back into `src/card-data.csv` as four new columns — `unitTestStatus`, `unitTestFailReason`, `browserTestStatus`, `browserTestFailReason` — preserving all existing columns and row order; pass rows have an empty reason, fail rows carry a concise note.
6. Meta-tests prove each framework actually fails on a missing definition and on a deliberately wrong expectation (guards against a green-but-useless suite).
7. The browser suite is wired into the project's test profiles so it runs in the standard dev/smoke workflow.
8. The framework is extensible: adding a new card requires only a test definition, not framework changes.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments and `docs/main-street`.
10. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unit tests are **integration tests**: real play states and turn progressions, not isolated pure-function calls alone.
- Deterministic: seeded `setupMainStreetGame`.
- The CSV is also consumed by `@balance-cards` (parser/`CSV_COLUMNS`/checksum) and the card-art pipeline — appended columns must not break existing tests (`tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts`, `csv-checksum.test.ts`, `balance-cards-csv-pipeline.test.ts`).
- The main-street root `vite.config.ts` currently defines only a `unit` project; browser execution needs a browser vitest project (Playwright + `@vitest/browser` are already devDependencies).
- Browser tests are context/GPU sensitive; run serially (`fileParallelism: false`).
- Do not modify `.pi/`, skill, or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Existing state

- `src/card-data.csv`: 174 cards, 46 columns; single source of truth.
- Engine APIs available: `setupMainStreetGame`, `executeWeekStart`, `executeAction`, `purchaseBusiness`, `buyAndPlaceBusiness`, `hireStaffCard`, `purchaseUpgrade`, `buyAndPlaceUpgrade`, `purchaseEvent`, `playBusinessFromHand`, `playUpgradeFromHand`, `playEventFromHand`, `endTurnHeadless`, `computePurchaseCostDiscount`, `computeUpgradeCostDiscount`, `refreshMarketCost`.
- Existing controlled-state test patterns: `tests/main-street/WeekGatedMarket.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts`.
- Existing browser boot pattern: `tests/e2e/main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts`.
- `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts` covers the balance tool, not live card behaviour.

## Desired change

Introduce a Main Street card verification framework under `tests/main-street/cards/` (shared registry + result writer + per-family definitions + combination definitions) with two sibling test suites — unit integration (Node) and browser integration (Playwright) — that write per-card results back into `src/card-data.csv`.

## Key files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestRegistry.ts` — parse CSV, discover cards, register/resolve per-card definitions
- `tests/main-street/cards/CardTestResultWriter.ts` — append `unitTest*` / `browserTest*` columns safely
- `tests/main-street/cards/definitions/{business,community-space,upgrade,staff,event,combinations}.ts` — per-card definitions
- `tests/main-street/cards/helpers/stateBuilders.ts` — shared controlled-state builders
- `tests/main-street/cards/unit/CardIntegration.test.ts`, `CardCombinations.test.ts`, `CardTestFramework.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/cards/browser/CardIntegration.browser.test.ts`, `CardCombinations.browser.test.ts`, `sceneHarness.ts`
- `vite.config.ts` — add a `browser` project (Playwright, Chromium)
- `src/card-data.csv` — four appended result columns
- `docs/main-street/` — document the framework and how to add a card test

## Related work

- **MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M** — Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects (discount implementation under test)
- **MS-0MUOSUN3O003MA1B** — Add comprehensive tests for Investor staff abilities (per-card test precedent)
- **MS-0MULW540X009EP9A** — CSV schema: add `upgradeCostDiscount` column to CsvRow and card-data.csv (CSV schema precedent)
- **MS-0MUMP92O9002772U** — Storyline behaviour regression harness (behaviour-harness precedent)
- **MS-0MUQUBITP000UUX6** — Net payback metric and contract test (contract-test precedent)
- **MS-0MTINKHUT009KHK5** — Market Card Cheat browser smoke test (browser boot pattern)
- Docs: `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** all 174 cards are individually reachable through engine APIs in a controllable state; some duration/choice events may need multi-turn drivage or scripted choices.
- **Assumption:** the scene exposes seams (or tolerates injected state) to build arbitrary boards without long scripted play.
- **Risk — CSV churn / race:** two runners writing the same CSV can clash and create noisy diffs. Mitigation: idempotent writer that only rewrites changed rows, or a merge writer; run writers sequentially.
- **Risk — slow/flaky browser suite:** 174 scene tests are heavy. Mitigation: minimal per-card scenarios, serial execution, warmed-up scene where safe, and keeping the suite in the dev profile rather than the fast unit profile.
- **Risk — false confidence:** a suite that passes without asserting. Mitigation: AC6 meta-tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** Monte-Carlo balance tuning and visual snapshot testing are out of scope — capture as linked work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: Should tests validate at the unit level, the browser level, or both?** — Answer (producer): "both, create two separate work items one for unit and one for browser. Note the unit tests must test against real play states and turn progressions — these are integration tests." Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Should the design be a parameterised test framework (one test definition per card) rather than 174 hand-written tests?** — Answer (producer): "Yes". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Should tests cover individual card effects only, or also combinations?** — Answer (producer): "Individual plus up to 3 combinations for validation". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Should every event card be tested, or only non-trivial events?** — Answer (producer): "Every card". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Where should results be reported?** — Answer (producer): "Results should be written into a new column in the CSV showing pass/fail and in the event of a fail a note on the problem." Follow-up answer: "Add columns". Source: interactive reply.
- **Q: Is a multi-turn integration pattern (setup → buy/play → advance turns → assert) acceptable?** — Answer (producer): "yes". Source: interactive reply.
- **Research:** the CSV is consumed by `@balance-cards` (`CSV_COLUMNS`, parser, checksum) and the card-art generator, so appended columns must stay backward compatible; the main-street root `vite.config.ts` has only a `unit` project today, so the browser child must add a browser project (Playwright, Chromium, already a devDependency). Evidence: `src/card-data.csv`, `core/src/balance-cards/csv.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, `package.json`, `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts`.
data.title: Card-level unit and browser integration test framework with CSV result reporting

# Plan Complete — Card-level unit and browser integration test framework with CSV result reporting

## Plan summary

This epic decomposes into **two producer-approved feature children** (producer answer to Q1: *"both, create two separate work items one for unit and one for browser"*; Q3: *"Individual plus up to 3 combinations"*; Q4: *"Every card"*; Q5: *"Add columns"*).

| # | Feature child | Scope | Depends on |
|---|---------------|-------|------------|
| 1 | **Unit integration card test framework + full card coverage (Node/Vitest)** — `MS-0MUXWGT7G009THBO` | Shared `CardTestRegistry` + per-family definitions + `CardTestResultWriter` (unit columns) + Node integration suites + meta-tests | — |
| 2 | **Browser integration card test framework + full card coverage (Vitest/Playwright)** — `MS-0MUXWH99P005TOOM` | Real `MainStreetScene` suites + scene harness + browser vitest project (unit columns reused) + meta-tests | 1 (via `wl dep`) |

### Parent AC → child coverage map

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|-----------|------------|
| AC1 discover 174 cards; missing definition = failure | Unit AC1, Browser AC1 |
| AC2 unit integration suite (setup → acquire/play → advance turns → assert) | Unit AC2 |
| AC3 browser integration suite (real scene, UI/state) | Browser AC1, AC2 |
| AC4 staff up to 3 combination tests | Unit AC3, Browser AC3 |
| AC5 four CSV columns (`unitTest*`, `browserTest*`), existing columns/order preserved | Unit AC4, Browser AC4 |
| AC6 meta-tests (missing definition, deliberately wrong expectation) | Unit AC6, Browser AC6 |
| AC7 browser suite wired into test profiles | Browser AC5 |
| AC8 extensibility (definition-only for a new card) | Unit AC5 |
| AC9 docs updated (`docs/main-street`, code comments) | Unit AC7, Browser AC7 |
| AC10 full project suite passes | Unit AC8, Browser AC8 |

Selected existing state verified this run: `src/card-data.csv` = 174 rows × 46 columns, families `event` 71, `upgrade` 39, `business` 31, `staff` 25, `community-space` 8 (matches parent AC1); `vite.config.ts` currently defines only the `unit` project; Playwright + `@vitest/browser` present in `devDependencies`; all referenced pre-existing files (`tests/main-street/WeekGatedMarket.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/main-street-cheat-smoke.browser.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts`, `core/src/balance-cards/csv.ts`, `tests/main-street/balance-cards.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/csv-checksum.test.ts`) exist.

## Approval gate

`plan-approval-gate` reports `request_approval: true` (effort **Large** scale, risk **High**). The feature plan is **not newly proposed in this run** — it was created and producer-approved in the prior planning session, evidenced by the recorded Appendix answers (Q1–Q6) and the two existing child work items. No re-approval was requested to avoid asking an already-answered question (idempotent re-run).

## Automated review stages

Finished Requirements & AC alignment review: every parent AC traces to at least one child AC and vice-versa; no invented, missing, or contradictory ACs; verified the CSV family counts referenced by AC1 (174 = 71+39+31+25+8).

Finished Completeness review: both feature children carry Problem statement, Users, Acceptance Criteria, Constraints, Existing state, Desired change, Key files, Related work and Risks.
